beginner.summary: No version control experience assumed. Participants learn to track changes, branch, merge, collaborate through pull requests and fix common mistakes.
prerequisites: Can edit text files in an editor
outcomes: Track and inspect changes with commits
Collaborate through remotes and pull requests

days.topic: Version Control Concepts and Git Setup
subtopics: git config: name, email and editor
Creating a repository with git init
The working tree, staging area and repository
days.lab_task: Create a repository for a small website, make five commits with clear messages, and add a .gitignore that excludes build output and editor files.
days.deliverable: Repository with five commits, a .gitignore and the git log output
checks: Shows five commits with clear messages
Create a file in the ignored build folder and run git status
Participant explains the difference between staged and unstaged changes

subtopics: git diff for unstaged and staged changes
days.lab_task: Use git log, diff, show and blame on a provided repository to answer ten questions such as who changed a line, when a function was added and what changed in a release.
days.deliverable: Answers to the ten questions with the command used for each
checks: Find the commit that introduced a given function
Correct commit ID with the command used
Show who last changed line 20 of a file
objectives: Find who changed what and when

days.lab_task: Build two features on separate branches, merge one with a fast-forward and the other with a merge commit, and show both in the history graph.
days.deliverable: Repository history graph and an explanation of each merge type
checks: Shows both feature branches and the merge commit
Explain why one merge was a fast-forward
Branch is deleted and commits remain in history
objectives: Merge with fast-forward and merge commits

days.lab_task: Create two branches that change the same lines, merge them, resolve the conflict keeping both changes correctly, and repeat with an abort.
days.deliverable: Resolved file, merge commit and notes on each conflict
checks: No conflict markers remain and both changes are kept
Run git merge --abort during a second conflict
Repository returns to the pre-merge state

subtopics: SSH keys and personal access tokens
days.lab_task: Push the website repository to GitHub over SSH, clone it into a second folder, make a change there, push it, and fetch it back into the first folder.
days.deliverable: GitHub repository link and the command transcript
checks: Clone the repository on another machine or folder
Push from the second folder and fetch in the first
First folder sees the new commit after merging
Participant explains that pull is fetch plus merge
objectives: Authenticate with SSH keys or tokens

subtopics: Writing a good pull request description
Merge, squash and rebase merge options
days.lab_task: In pairs, each open a pull request for a feature, review the partner's pull request with at least three comments, address the feedback, and merge.
days.deliverable: Two merged pull requests with review comments and follow-up commits
checks: Each has review comments and a follow-up commit
Explains what changed, why and how to test
Participant explains squash or merge commit choice
objectives: Give and act on code review

subtopics: git restore for working tree changes
When not to rewrite shared history
days.lab_task: Work through six mistake scenarios (wrong file staged, bad last commit message, bad pushed commit, lost commit after reset, unfinished work before switching branch, deleted branch) and fix each safely.
days.deliverable: Command log for each scenario with the reason for the chosen fix
checks: Branch is back with its commits

subtopics: Rebasing a feature branch on main
days.lab_task: Rebase a feature branch onto an updated main, resolve a conflict during the rebase, and squash six small commits into two meaningful ones before opening a pull request.
days.deliverable: History before and after the rebase and the pull request
checks: Feature commits sit on top of main in two clear commits
Explain why not to rebase a shared branch
objectives: Clean up commits with interactive rebase

days.lab_task: Simulate a team release with three features, a release branch and an urgent hotfix using Git flow, then repeat the same work with trunk-based development and compare.
days.deliverable: Two history graphs and a comparison note
checks: Fix reaches both the release and main
Covers merge effort, release speed and risk
Participant explains releasing incomplete work safely
objectives: Choose a strategy for a team

days.lab_task: Tag three releases of the website with semantic versions, publish GitHub releases with generated notes, and check out an old release to reproduce a bug.
days.deliverable: Tags, release pages and the reproduced bug notes
checks: Has notes listing included pull requests

days.lab_task: Plan a small sprint on a GitHub Projects board with issue templates, labels and a milestone, then close three issues through linked pull requests.
days.deliverable: Project board, templates and three closed issues
checks: Create an issue from the template
objectives: Track work with issues and boards

days.lab_task: Protect main so it needs one approving review, a passing check and code owner review for the docs folder, and prove a direct push is rejected.
days.deliverable: Ruleset configuration, CODEOWNERS file and the rejected push
checks: Open a pull request changing docs

days.topic: Git with IDEs and GUI Tools
subtopics: Line endings across Windows and Linux
days.lab_task: Repeat a branch, partial commit, conflict and pull request workflow entirely in VS Code, configure a visual merge tool, and fix a line-ending problem.
days.deliverable: Screenshots of each step and the .gitattributes file
checks: Stage only half of a changed file
Commit contains only the chosen lines
Resolve a conflict with the merge tool
Commit from Windows and check out on Linux
objectives: Use Git from editors and GUI tools

days.topic: Working with Large Files and Repositories
subtopics: Removing large files with git filter-repo
days.lab_task: Move design files to Git LFS, find and remove a large file accidentally committed earlier, and compare clone times with shallow and sparse options.
days.deliverable: Before and after repository sizes, LFS configuration and clone timing table
checks: Check the repository size after clean-up
Large file is gone from history
Shallow and sparse clones are faster, with figures
objectives: Store large files with Git LFS
Speed up work in large repositories

days.topic: Removing Secrets and Sensitive Data from Git
subtopics: Why deleting a file is not enough
days.lab_task: Find a planted API key in a repository's history with gitleaks, rotate it, remove it from all history with git filter-repo, and add push protection and a pre-commit scanner.
days.deliverable: Scan reports before and after, rewrite commands and the protection settings
checks: Try to push a new key
Push protection or the pre-commit hook blocks it
Participant explains that copies of history may already exist

subtopics: Running linters and tests before commit
days.lab_task: Add pre-commit hooks for formatting, linting and secret scanning, and a commit-msg hook that enforces Conventional Commits, shared through the repository.
days.deliverable: Hook configuration and examples of blocked and accepted commits
checks: Hooks work with one documented command

days.topic: Debugging with Git: bisect and blame
subtopics: git bisect start, good and bad
Automating bisect with a test script
git log -L for a function's history
Restoring a single file from history
Writing a regression test after finding the cause
days.lab_task: Use git bisect with an automated test to find the commit that broke a feature in a 200-commit repository, then restore the correct code and add a regression test.
days.deliverable: Bisect log, the offending commit and the fix with its test
checks: Run git bisect run with the test
Run the regression test on the fix
Show the history of one function with git log -L
Lists the commits that changed it

days.lab_task: Add a shared library to two projects first as a submodule and then as a subtree, update it in both ways, and write a recommendation for the team.
days.deliverable: Both repository setups, update logs and a recommendation
checks: Library is fetched with the documented command
Change appears without extra commands for users

days.lab_task: Create a commit by hand using git hash-object, update-index, write-tree and commit-tree, then point a branch at it and explain each object you created.
days.deliverable: Command transcript and an annotated diagram of the objects
checks: Run git log on the new branch
Show the tree of the commit with git cat-file -p
Blob, tree, commit and branch relationships are correct

days.topic: Beginner Capstone: Team Project with a Git Workflow
subtopics: Feature branches and reviewed pull requests
days.lab_task: In teams of three, build a small website with protected main, hooks, issues, at least six reviewed pull requests, one resolved conflict, one hotfix and a tagged release, then present the history.
days.deliverable: Team repository, project board, release page and a 10-minute history walkthrough
checks: Each member authored and reviewed pull requests
Fix reached main and the release through the chosen strategy
Tagged with semantic version and notes
objectives: Run a complete team Git workflow
Combine branching, review, protection and releases

intermediate.summary: For people who use Git daily. Covers advanced history editing, repository administration, GitHub automation, security, monorepo scale and recovering from serious mistakes.
prerequisites: Uses branches, merges, rebases and pull requests every day
Has worked in a team repository with protected branches
outcomes: Administer repositories and organisations on GitHub or GitLab
Automate repository work with Actions, APIs and the GitHub CLI
Run Git at scale for large codebases and teams

days.topic: Advanced Interactive Rebase and History Editing
days.lab_task: Turn a messy 15-commit branch into five clean, individually passing commits using fixup, split and reorder, verified with rebase exec running the tests at each step.
days.deliverable: History before and after and the rebase exec log
checks: Run tests at every commit with rebase exec
Compare final code with the messy branch

days.lab_task: Maintain two release branches: backport three fixes from main, resolve a conflict in one, and automate future backports with a labelled pull request workflow.
days.deliverable: Backport commits, automation workflow and an automated backport pull request
checks: Label a merged pull request for backport
Automation opens a backport pull request

days.lab_task: Set up an organisation with three teams, organisation rulesets for all repositories, a repository template, and find a permission change in the audit log.
days.deliverable: Organisation configuration, ruleset definitions and the audit log finding
checks: Create a repository from the template
Has the standard files and rules applied
Push to main in any repository
Find who changed a team's access
Audit log shows the actor and time

days.lab_task: Mirror a GitHub repository to GitLab, set up protected branches and approval rules there, complete a merge request, and compare the workflow with GitHub.
days.deliverable: Mirror configuration, merge request and a comparison table
checks: Change appears in the GitLab mirror
Merge without the required approval in GitLab

days.topic: Automating Repositories with GitHub CLI and APIs
subtopics: Authentication with fine-grained tokens and GitHub Apps
days.lab_task: Write a script with a GitHub App token that finds stale pull requests across an organisation, comments on them, and opens a pull request adding a missing CODEOWNERS file to each repository.
days.deliverable: Script, run log and the opened pull requests
checks: Run the script in dry-run mode
Lists what it would change without changing anything
Comments and pull requests are created as listed
Exceed the rate limit in a test
objectives: Automate GitHub with the CLI and APIs

days.lab_task: Set up SSH commit signing, require signed commits on main, sign commits made by a CI bot, and verify the history.
days.deliverable: Signing configuration, ruleset and verification output
checks: Push an unsigned commit to a protected branch
Check a bot commit on GitHub

days.topic: Repository Security: Dependabot, Code Scanning and Secret Scanning
days.lab_task: Enable Dependabot, CodeQL and secret scanning on a vulnerable sample repository, fix the three highest-severity findings, and configure grouped dependency updates.
days.deliverable: Security configuration, fixed findings and Dependabot pull requests
objectives: Find vulnerabilities in code and dependencies

subtopics: Partial clone and sparse checkout in practice
days.lab_task: Clone a large monorepo with Scalar and sparse checkout, measure status and log times before and after maintenance settings, and set up a merge queue.
days.deliverable: Timing table, configuration and a merge queue run
checks: Faster with fsmonitor and maintenance, with figures
Check out only two project folders
Working tree contains only those folders
Add two pull requests to the merge queue
Both are tested together and merged in order
objectives: Keep Git fast in large repositories
Use sparse checkout and partial clone

subtopics: Migrating from SVN or TFVC to Git
days.lab_task: Split a folder out of a monorepo into its own repository with full history, merge two small repositories into one with history, and validate both.
days.deliverable: Migration commands, resulting repositories and validation evidence
checks: Run git log on the split repository
History of that folder is preserved
Run git log on the merged repository
Both histories are present under their folders
Compare file contents with the originals

days.lab_task: Automate releases so merging to main computes the next version from commit messages, generates a changelog, creates a signed tag and publishes a GitHub release.
days.deliverable: Release workflow and two automated releases

days.lab_task: Run an inner source exercise where teams contribute to another team's repository through forks, following its guidelines, with maintainers reviewing within an agreed time.
days.deliverable: Contribution guide, merged contributions and a contribution health report
checks: Fork is up to date without merge noise
Explains setup, standards and review times
Shows review times and contributor counts

subtopics: Restoring from reflog on another machine
days.lab_task: Recover from five serious incidents prepared by the trainer, including a force-push over main and a corrupted object, and write a short incident note for one.
days.deliverable: Recovery log for each incident and one incident note
checks: States impact, cause, fix and prevention

days.topic: Git Workflows for Infrastructure and GitOps
subtopics: Repositories as the source of truth
days.lab_task: Design a GitOps repository for three environments, promote a change from dev to prod through pull requests, and protect the prod folder with code owners and checks.
days.deliverable: Repository structure, promotion pull requests and protection settings
checks: Change prod without code owner approval
Same commit content moves dev to test to prod
Find who approved a prod change
Git history and pull request show it
objectives: Use Git as an audit trail

days.lab_task: Split a large change into three stacked pull requests, add automated lint comments to reviews, and assign reviewers automatically with load balancing.
days.deliverable: Stacked pull requests, review automation and review metrics
checks: Each is small and reviewable on its own
Bot comments on the exact line

days.topic: Git Server Hooks and Platform Policies
days.lab_task: On a self-hosted Git server, write a pre-receive hook that blocks files over 10 MB and commits without a ticket ID, and test it with good and bad pushes.
days.deliverable: Hook code, tests and push results
checks: Push a commit without a ticket ID
objectives: Enforce policy on the server side

days.topic: Collaboration Analytics and Engineering Metrics from Git
days.lab_task: Pull a year of pull request and commit data from a sample organisation, compute cycle time, review time and hotspots, and present findings with recommendations.
days.deliverable: Data script, dashboard and findings
checks: Compute median pull request cycle time

days.topic: Self-Hosting Git: GitLab and Gitea Administration
days.lab_task: Install a self-hosted Git server with SSO, back it up, upgrade it, restore it on a new machine, and verify repositories and users survive.
days.deliverable: Installation runbook, backup and restore record and upgrade log
checks: Repositories, users and settings are intact
objectives: Back up, restore and upgrade it

days.topic: Git for Data, Documentation and Non-Code Assets
days.lab_task: Version a documentation site and a dataset: publish docs from Git automatically, track a dataset with DVC, and review a notebook change with readable diffs.
days.deliverable: Docs pipeline, DVC configuration and a reviewed notebook pull request
checks: Check out an old dataset version with DVC

days.topic: Git Training and Standards for an Organisation
days.lab_task: Write a Git standards document and repository template for a 200-developer organisation, pilot it with one team, and collect feedback.
days.deliverable: Standards document, template repository and pilot feedback summary
checks: Create a repository from the template
Cover branching, commits, reviews and security
Lists changes made from the pilot
objectives: Set Git standards for an organisation

days.topic: Intermediate Capstone: Repository Platform for an Engineering Organisation
days.lab_task: Set up an organisation's repository platform with rulesets, templates, signing, security scanning, release and backport automation, a merge queue and metrics, then present it.
days.deliverable: Organisation configuration, automation repositories, metrics dashboard and a 15-minute demo
checks: Create a new repository from the template
All rules and scans apply automatically
Shows cycle time and review time
objectives: Design a repository platform for many teams

advanced.summary: For engineers who own source control for large organisations. Covers Git internals, performance at extreme scale, supply chain integrity, compliance, platform migrations and source control strategy.
prerequisites: Administers repositories or a Git platform for many teams
Comfortable with history editing, automation and repository security
Has scripted against Git hosting APIs
outcomes: Diagnose and tune Git at the object and protocol level
Secure source code supply chains with verifiable provenance
Run compliance, retention and audit for source control
Lead platform migrations and source control strategy

days.topic: Git Object Model and Packfile Internals
days.lab_task: Analyse a large repository's packfiles, find the objects that dominate its size, repack it with tuned settings, and measure clone and fetch speed before and after.
days.deliverable: Analysis report, repack settings and timing table
objectives: Explain how Git stores and compresses data

days.topic: Git Transfer Protocols and Server Performance
days.lab_task: Trace a fetch with packet tracing, then cut CI clone load on a server by 70% using bundle URIs, shallow fetches and a local mirror, measuring server load before and after.
days.deliverable: Protocol trace annotations and a load reduction report
checks: Compare server load during a simulated CI storm
At least 70% lower or the gap is explained
Clone uses the bundle then fetches the rest

subtopics: Virtual file systems and Scalar background maintenance
Build system integration with sparse checkout
days.lab_task: Generate a synthetic repository with a million files, make common operations fast with sparse index and Scalar, and document the limits you hit.
days.deliverable: Benchmark results, configuration and a limits report
checks: Compare git status time with and without sparse index
Each limit has a measured threshold
Check a teammate can reproduce the setup
Documented steps work on a clean machine

subtopics: Signed commits and tags at organisation scale
Branch protection as a security control
days.lab_task: Design source integrity controls for an organisation, enforce keyless signing with gitsign, link build provenance to signed commits, and detect a simulated tampered commit.
days.deliverable: Control design, signing configuration, provenance evidence and tamper detection result
checks: Verify a release back to its signed commit
Maps controls to SLSA source requirements

days.topic: Compliance, Retention and Legal Holds for Source Control
subtopics: Regulatory requirements for source and change history
days.lab_task: Stream the audit log to a SIEM, build an evidence report proving reviewed changes for one quarter, and design retention and legal hold procedures.
days.deliverable: Audit streaming configuration, evidence report and procedures
checks: Find a ruleset bypass in the SIEM
Event appears with actor and time
Every production change has a reviewer distinct from the author
objectives: Meet compliance needs for source control

subtopics: Migrating between GitHub, GitLab, Bitbucket and Azure Repos
Migrating issues, pull requests and metadata
Wave planning across hundreds of repositories
days.lab_task: Plan the migration of 300 repositories between platforms, migrate a pilot wave of 10 with metadata, validate them automatically, and report issues found.
days.deliverable: Migration plan, pilot results and validation report
checks: Run the validation script on the pilot
Commits, branches, tags and pull requests match
Orders repositories by dependencies and risk
Commits are attributed to the right users
objectives: Migrate metadata as well as code

days.topic: Repository Governance Automation at Organisation Scale
days.lab_task: Manage settings for 200 repositories as code, detect and fix drift automatically, archive inactive repositories after owner confirmation, and report compliance.
days.deliverable: Settings repository, drift automation and a compliance report
checks: Only confirmed inactive repositories are archived
Shows compliance per repository and owner

days.lab_task: Build a GitHub App that enforces a pull request size policy and labels pull requests by changed areas, with idempotent webhook handling and tests.
days.deliverable: App code, tests and a demo on a test organisation
checks: App comments and sets a failing check

days.topic: Merge Strategies and Integration at Scale
days.lab_task: Simulate 200 pull requests a day with 5% flaky tests through a merge queue, tune batch size and retry settings, and report trunk health before and after.
days.deliverable: Simulation results, tuned settings and trunk health report
checks: Higher throughput after tuning, with figures
Shows red-trunk time and revert rate

subtopics: What must be recovered: code, metadata, settings, secrets
Backup strategies for hosted and self-hosted platforms
days.lab_task: Back up an organisation's repositories, issues and settings, then restore them to a clean environment in a timed exercise and document gaps.
days.deliverable: Backup design, restore runbook and the timed exercise report
checks: Compare restore time with the target
Within target or the gap is explained
Lists anything that could not be restored
objectives: Plan disaster recovery for source control
Back up metadata as well as code

days.topic: Insider Risk and Access Management for Code
days.lab_task: Detect a simulated mass-clone by a departing employee from audit data, design just-in-time admin access, and write an offboarding procedure that removes access within an hour.
days.deliverable: Detection query, access design and offboarding procedure
checks: Run the offboarding procedure on a test user
All access removed within an hour
objectives: Reduce insider risk for source code

days.topic: Source Control for Regulated and Air-Gapped Environments
days.lab_task: Move changes between a connected and an air-gapped Git server with signed bundles, verify integrity on the other side, and document the approval steps.
days.deliverable: Transfer procedure, signed bundles and verification evidence
checks: Apply a bundle on the air-gapped server

days.topic: Cost and Capacity Planning for Git Platforms
subtopics: CI minutes linked to repository activity
days.lab_task: Build a cost and capacity model for a Git platform serving 1,000 developers, find three savings, and forecast the next two years of storage and CI use.
days.deliverable: Cost model, savings proposals and forecast
checks: Breaks costs into seats, storage, CI and bandwidth
Has current cost, change and saving

days.lab_task: Measure developer friction in a sample organisation with a survey and Git telemetry, pick the top two problems, implement improvements and measure the effect.
days.deliverable: Friction analysis, implemented improvements and before and after metrics
checks: Top problems are backed by data
Ready in minutes with standards applied

subtopics: AI code suggestions and review assistants
days.lab_task: Write an organisation policy for AI-assisted coding, configure guardrails in a repository, and run a review exercise comparing AI-assisted and manual changes.
days.deliverable: Policy, repository configuration and the review exercise results
checks: Covers data, licences, review and accountability
Content exclusions and required reviews are set

days.lab_task: Respond to a simulated compromised personal access token used to push a malicious commit: contain, revoke, find all affected repositories, clean up and report.
days.deliverable: Incident timeline, list of affected repositories, clean-up record and report
checks: Includes root cause and preventive controls

days.topic: Designing Branching and Release Models for Many Products
days.lab_task: Design branching and release models for five products with different cadences and support terms, automate release branch creation, and simulate a quarter of releases.
days.deliverable: Model designs, automation and simulation results
checks: Releases and backports follow each product's model
Each product's model matches its cadence and support term
Compatible versions used by each product
objectives: Design release models for many products

subtopics: Security, scale, cost and usability criteria
days.lab_task: Review another team's capstone source control platform design, write two decision records for its biggest risks, and present recommendations with evidence.
days.deliverable: Review report, two decision records and a 10-minute presentation
checks: Each high risk has evidence and a recommendation
Options, criteria and the reason for the choice
Defended with cost and risk evidence

days.lab_task: Assess a provided organisation's source control maturity, propose a consolidation and improvement roadmap, and present it to a mock leadership panel.
days.deliverable: Maturity assessment, roadmap and presentation
checks: Each area has evidence and a level
Items have outcomes, owners and metrics
Budget and risk questions answered with evidence

days.topic: Advanced Capstone: Enterprise Source Control Platform
days.lab_task: Design and prototype an enterprise source control platform covering scale, integrity, governance, compliance, migration, recovery, developer experience and cost, then defend it to a review board.
days.deliverable: Architecture document, working prototype, integrity and recovery test evidence, cost model and a 20-minute review presentation
checks: Unsigned or tampered changes are blocked
Costs are broken down and justified
objectives: Design an enterprise source control platform
Prove integrity, recovery and cost with evidence
Defend the design to a review board
